item.description: Spokane Mayor Lisa Brown called the blazes burning through the area the "worst natural disaster our region has faced."

item.title: London building outdoor gyms with knives taken off streets
item.description: More than ten tons of weapons from Britain's streets have been melted down and transformed into outdoor gyms across London. CBS News' Tina Kraus reports.

item.title: Dog rescue hires a cat to help boost adoptions
item.description: Muttville Senior Dog Rescue in San Francisco has brought on a cat to help determine how open the adoptable canines are to living with a feline. Itay Hod reports.

item.title: New treatment for advanced melanoma uses tumor to fight the disease
item.description: A treatment for advanced melanoma that's newly approved by the FDA is giving cancer patients new hope. Tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte, or "TIL" therapy, uses an individual's own tumor to help fight the disease. CBS News' Natalie Brand reports.

item.title: Some in Gen Z ditching smartphones
item.description: Gen Z grew up glued to smartphones, but a growing number are choosing to disconnect. They're ditching social media and, in some cases, their smartphones altogether. CBS News' Maya Blackstone reports.

item.title: Revisiting Herbert Hoover's legacy as his presidential library reopens
item.description: In West Branch, Iowa, the newly reimagined Herbert Hoover Presidential Library and Museum wants to shed a fresh light on what historians consider a mixed legacy. Lana Zak reports.

item.title: A bicycle class for adults who never learned how to ride
item.description: Most Americans learn to ride a bike as children, but for those who were never taught, learning as an adult can be intimidating. CBS News' Michael George visited a cycling class where you're never too old to learn.

item.title: DOJ to dismiss Reflecting Pool vandalism charges, citing "botched installation"
item.description: Federal prosecutors moved to dismiss an indictment charging U.S. Olympic canoeist David Hearn with ripping the bottom of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, saying the damage was caused by "botched installation and not vandalism."

item.title: D.C. Reflecting Pool saga continues as Trump slams Pirro for saying contractors caused damage
item.description: The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool is now drained of water and awaiting repairs, as a feud within the Trump administration spills into the open. President Trump and Interior Secretary Doug Burgum are both rejecting the conclusion by U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro that contractors caused the pool to peel. Olivia Rinaldi reports.

item.title: U.S.-Iran negotiations set to begin Monday, Trump says after calling off strikes
item.description: President Trump said negotiations with Iran are set to begin Monday after announcing on Saturday that he canceled a pending attack on Iran.

item.title: Trump says outline of Iran deal agreed to, mediators say otherwise, strikes on hold for now
item.description: President Trump has called off new attacks on Iran for the time being, insisting an end to the war is close. He's also again calling for the "immediate" re-opening of the Strait of Hormuz. Imtiaz Tyab reports.

item.title: Twin Falls In-N-Out shooting suspect identified after 3 killed, 7 wounded
item.description: The suspect, identified as 24-year-old Chad Williams, died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound, police said.

item.title: New details on deadly In-N-Out shooting
item.description: New details are emerging about this weekend's deadly mass shooting at an In-N-Out restaurant in Twin Falls, Idaho. At least three people were killed in the attack and seven others wounded. Lindsey Reiser reports.

item.title: Mass evacuations underway as wildfires bear down on Spokane, Washington
item.description: Explosive wildfires in Spokane, Washington, have destroyed more than 600 structures, many of them within the city limits. The fast-moving flames led to mass evacuations and chaos, as families fled their homes. Adam Yamaguchi reports and Andrew Kozak looks at the forecast and the record heat threatening 50 million Americans.

item.title: ICE detentions set Trump-era high in July, as immigration crackdown widens
item.description: Detentions by Immigration and Customs Enforcement set a monthly record high for the second Trump administration in July, internal agency data obtained by CBS News shows, as ICE widened its crackdown.
